newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian defence aide says joining NATO not option.
newsitem.headline: Russian defence aide says joining NATO not option.

text.p: A top Kremlin defence adviser, responding to a colleague's suggestion that Russia might end its dispute with NATO by joining the western alliance, said on Wednesday there was little point in discussing such an option.

"The NATO countries are not giving any signs that they would like to invite Russia in as a full member of NATO in the near future," Yuri Baturin, secretary of the Defence Council, told Ekho Mosky radio.
"The issue exists on a theoretical plane. On the practical plane, it's not worth raising the issue," he said.

On Tuesday, Ivan Rybkin, secretary of the Kremlin Security Council was quoted as saying he was in favour of Russia joining NATO's political organisation and later even taking part in the military structures of the alliance.

But it seemed the idea, which Rybkin had expressed before, was a personal one rather than a change in Moscow's position. Russia opposes the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation's (NATO) plans to expand into eastern Europe.
Baturin said Russian membership of NATO would change the organisation from a closed one to an open system of Atlantic or even Eurasian security. But he ruled it out as a possibility.

He went on to complain of pressure being put on Russia to soften its opposition to NATO expansion and said Moscow could find itself pressed to drop its objections by western nations at next month's Lisbon conference on European security.
"This is unacceptable for us. Russia will never agree to pat little formulas which would mean an indirect recognition by Russia of NATO expansion," Baturin said.
